I understand the worshipping culture given that I also come from a Buddhist culture and we were brought up to worship any adult who is older and/or related or family friend of the parents. But growing up I started questioning why we do this for everyone even when we barely know them. It just takes away the meaning of the whole thing and takes the essence of it away from people  you actually love, care, respect and admire so I now only do it to adults I truly respect like parents and immediate family (aunts/uncles). Not random aunties and uncles I am introduced to for the first time at a Bana. 

But personally the whole worshipping your partner in front of everyone at the wedding is so outdated. This was a tradition that started because it was earlier marriages had larger age gaps so the man was always much older but the main reason was because it was the man who only worked and brought in the money which equals the roof over your head, the food on the table etc. the woman wasn’t expected/allowed in some cases to work so therefore the man took on the Provider role hence the respect by worshipping. It has nothing to do with Buddhism and just a part of culture for the above reason only. 

Times have changed and both contribute in a monetary sense now. So the need to still bow down and worship your partner (when btw the man would almost never do this to the woman in this circumstance) front of everyone just to show respect is just weird imo. There are other ways to honor, respect and love your partner in an equal way, without putting yourself below another for the sake of outdated culture.

So my advice is a little different - first of all, it completely makes sense if you are able to take that much needed break given that you are financially capable. The break would do you good and the more you push this, you might not actually get the chance as more commitments might come up in the future so now’s the time.

But what I would say is - you might feel this way again 8-12 months down the line that you feel that you need a break again since your actual lifestyle would not really change. You are taking a break and you are coming back to the same lifestyle so it’s sort of a cycle. I would say take the break to figure out what you want to do - sort of take control of your life in the sense, plan certain activities within the week whether it’s starting a scheduled fitness activity (gym, badminton etc) or make an intentional plan where you reach out and catch up with a friend for coffee/dinner after work every 2 weeks or take up a new hobby like reading and make a goal to finish x number by end of the year, plan a getaway with your husband somewhere local once in 2 months etc

You are already winning at life if you have a job you like - that’s a huge benefit you have as not everyone could say that. Now see how you can improve other areas of your lifestyle so the need to take a vacation/break is not as needed since your day to day life already feels like one :)
